tasks.title: Extend the repo-wide census to letter-spacing and border widths, with no exception list
acceptance: src/renderer/src/__tests__/hygiene.test.ts carries a repo-wide rule asserting that no `letter-spacing` declaration in any `*.module.css` under src/renderer/src has a value outside the `--oc-tracking-*` family, scanning the population the frozen contract's `CensusScope` names and carrying no exception list of any kind. The assertion is two-sided in the contract's `CensusAssertionShape`: the offender list is compared against the empty list.

The same file carries a repo-wide rule asserting that no value of any property in the frozen contract's `BORDER_WIDTH_PROPERTIES` carries a raw length, over the same population, with no exception list, and two-sided in the same shape.

Both new rules read declarations with the anchored reader the contract's `DeclarationReader` names, so a longhand cannot be read as the shorthand it is spelled inside and a custom property cannot be read as a property.

The tracking rule's matcher test flags every sample in the contract's `TRACKING_MUST_FLAG` and flags none in `TRACKING_MUST_PASS`, both directions asserted in the file rather than described. The wrong-family sample `letter-spacing: var(--oc-space-2)` is the one that matters: a predicate testing only for `var(` passes it, which is the defect C3's `WEIGHT_TOKEN` regex exists to close.

The border rule's matcher test flags every sample in the contract's `BORDER_MUST_FLAG` and flags none in `BORDER_MUST_PASS`, both directions asserted in the file. `border-radius: 4px` is the near-miss that matters: 69 `border-radius` declarations exist in this tree and not one of them may enter the offender set.

The tracking rule is shown able to fail against the real tree, not only against synthetic strings: inject a bare `letter-spacing` into a `*.module.css` OUTSIDE `beachcomber/`, `helm/` and `shell/`, run `npx vitest run src/renderer/src/__tests__/hygiene.test.ts`, report the failing assertion and its message, then revert. Injecting outside those three roots is the point — it is the scope trap this whole section exists to close.
The border rule is shown able to fail the same way: inject `border: 1px solid var(--oc-border)` into a `*.module.css` outside those three roots, run the same command, report the failure, then revert.

Both new rules scan the list the existing census guard covers, so neither can pass by scanning nothing — the contract's `CensusSelfCheck` states what that guard asserts, and this criterion is met by the new rules walking that same list, or by an equivalent guard of their own if they do not.

Neither new rule introduces a constant enumerating tolerated declarations, and no such constant exists anywhere in the file as this task leaves it. Emptying the last of them was T4's work, and re-creating one for a different property would reinstate exactly what this session removed.

AMENDMENT A1 (escalation E2). The file carries a third repo-wide rule asserting that every `var(--oc-*)` reference in any `*.module.css` under src/renderer/src is TERMINATED by one of: a space, `,`, `)`, `;`, `}`, or end-of-line. Two-sided (offenders compared against the empty list), no exception list, over the same population as the other two censuses, and read with the same anchored reader. It must flag `border: var(--oc-border-hairline)solid red` and `border: var(--oc-border-hairline)dashed red`; it must NOT flag `border: var(--oc-border-hairline) solid red`, `box-shadow: 0 0 0 var(--oc-space-1), 0 0 0 var(--oc-space-2)`, `padding: var(--oc-space-2);` or `grid-template-columns: var(--oc-a) var(--oc-b)`. Both directions asserted in the file rather than described. This closes a defect class with NO detector in this repo: T2's first pass produced `var(--oc-border-hairline)solid` on all 14 of its lines — invalid CSS the browser discards entirely, so every one of those borders would have vanished on screen — and the raw-length census passed it cleanly, as did the full pods suite at 31/31. Verified by the orchestrator: no CSS parser exists anywhere under src/ or tests/, and `styles/tokens.test.ts` checks only that token NAMES match the frozen TOKENS map, never that a usage is syntactically live.

That third rule is shown able to fail against the real tree, not only against synthetic strings: inject the dead form into a `*.module.css` OUTSIDE `beachcomber/`, `helm/` and `shell/`, run `npx vitest run src/renderer/src/__tests__/hygiene.test.ts`, report the failing assertion and its message, then revert.

No test name in this file claims more than its test checks, which test.md's Naming rule requires ('The name must not claim more than the test checks. A name broader than its assertions misleads every later reader'). A name saying 'everywhere' or 'with no exception list' must be carried by a rule that walks the whole population and tolerates nothing.

Every count and every universal this task adds to or edits in the file's prose is true of the tree as this task leaves it, including the header bullet list at af12edc lines 16-17, which scopes the border-width and letter-spacing rules to `beachcomber/`, `helm/` and `shell/` — a scope this task's change makes false.

`npm test` passes on a quiescent tree, with the test-file and test counts REPORTED AS MEASURED from that run's own output rather than asserted against the handoff brief's 141 files and 2240 tests, which this session has not re-verified. Report the same two numbers measured the same way at the session base af12edc, and the delta between them.

`npm run typecheck` exits 0, covering both programs (`typecheck:node` over tsconfig.node.json and `typecheck:web` over tsconfig.web.json). Report each program's exit code separately: vitest transpiles without typechecking, so a green suite is not evidence for this.

tasks.title: Extend the Electron hand-run driver so the converted values are seen rendered
acceptance: A driver at .dir-sdlc/handruns/2026-09-30-electron-handrun/driver/run-token-sweep.mjs drives the real built Electron app through Playwright against the sandboxed home, reusing driver/lib.mjs and driver/sandbox.mjs as driver/run-c3.mjs does, with USERPROFILE/APPDATA/LOCALAPPDATA/TEMP redirected so the real ~/.claude is not touched. Report the sandbox root the run used.

The run is driven against a build produced from THIS SESSION'S worktree, not from the main checkout. `lib.mjs`'s `repoRoot` resolves relative to the driver file, so a driver executed from the main checkout's copy would launch a build with none of this session's conversions in it and would confirm nothing. State which checkout was built, and name the commit or the converted declaration observed in the built bundle that proves it.
`npm run build` completes in that worktree, which runs `typecheck:node` and `typecheck:web` ahead of the bundle. Report its exit code.

`.railHeading` is on screen and its computed `letter-spacing` is MEASURED in the running window. The element is the `<h2 id="lane-rail-heading">` rendered by src/renderer/src/lanes/LaneRail.tsx:70. The measured value equals 0.04 times the element's own computed `font-size`, within sub-pixel rounding, and is strictly less than 0.06 times it. Compare against the element's measured font-size rather than a hardcoded pixel value. This is the session's one authorised visible change, and it is the element no hand-run has ever rendered.

That probe is shown able to discriminate: override `letter-spacing` back to `0.06em` on the same element in-page, re-probe, and report a strictly larger measured value. A probe that has only ever reported the value it expected has not been shown to measure anything — this project's recurring defect is a check that cannot report.

AMENDED A2 (escalation E3). At least one converted border declaration is measured in the running window and computes the SAME used width as a literal `1px` measured live in the same window, naming the element and the stylesheet it comes from. The comparison is against a reference element created and measured in that window, never against the string `1px`. Original text, frozen at Gate 2: 'At least one converted border declaration is measured in the running window with a computed border width of 1px, naming the element and the stylesheet it comes from.' That text was unsatisfiable: Chromium quantises used border widths to whole device pixels, so on the display under test no 1px border computes to `1px` — a declared literal included, measuring 0.8px on a ladder fitting floor(declared x 1.25)/1.25 exactly. It also contradicted criterion 4 of this same task, which forbids comparing against a hardcoded pixel value for the analogous measurement; the method criterion 4 mandates is the one that makes this criterion's intent measurable.

That border probe is shown able to discriminate on TOKEN RESOLUTION, which is the failure a passing suite cannot see: override `--oc-border-hairline` in-page to a value that does not resolve as a length, re-probe the same element, and report the different computed width observed. A token that failed to resolve computes to a width the probe must distinguish from 1px.

The findings document records, for each of the 7 converted stylesheets (lanes/LaneRail, pods/DeletePodDialog, pods/NewPodDialog, pods/PodBar, shell/EmptyWorkspace, shell/WorkspaceLayout, transcript/Transcript), either a measured computed value on a converted declaration in that file or an explicit statement that no converted site in it could be reached, with the reason. No site is reported as verified unless it was measured. Recording a limit satisfies this criterion; claiming a site that was never on screen does not.

The findings document records, for each of the 3 converted `letter-spacing` sites (lanes/LaneRail `.railHeading`, pods/PodBar `.bypassBadge`, transcript/Transcript line 181 at af12edc), either its measured computed value or the reason it could not be reached. Two of the three plausibly need application state the driver cannot create — a bypass-permission Pod and live transcript content — and recording that is a pass.

The findings document carries a section stating what the run did NOT prove, in the shape FINDINGS-C3.md uses. A run that reports only its passes is this project's instrument problem in another form, and C3's own honest limit — 3 of 10 semibold sites rendered — is the reason this task exists.

Every count in the findings document and in the run's report is attributed to the command or the probe that produced it, and every harness failure is recorded as a harness failure, distinguished from an application defect. C3's first pass would have reported 20/23 on three harness faults.

The task's diff touches nothing outside .dir-sdlc/handruns/2026-09-30-electron-handrun/, shown by `git status --porcelain`. In particular no file under src/ is modified: an in-page override is a runtime probe and is never committed.
